channel.title: Nature Physics
channel.description: Nature Physics offers news and reviews alongside top-quality research papers in a monthly publication, covering the entire spectrum of physics. Physics addresses the properties and interactions of matter and energy, and plays a key role in the development of a broad range of technologies. To reflect this, Nature Physics covers all areas of pure and applied physics research. The journal focuses on core physics disciplines, but is also open to a broad range of topics whose central theme falls within the bounds of physics.

item.title: [7] Rotation through sound
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Franklin J. Vivanco

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Studies quantized circulation in strongly correlated matter using phononic interferometry.

Tags: #stronglycorrelated #superfluid #phonons

Abstract: Detecting quantized circulation in strongly correlated matter is challenging. Now it has been shown that phononic interferometry can reveal the quantized angular momentum of a strongly interacting rotating superfluid.

item.title: [6] Long-lived phonons from resonators with reduced surface interactions
item.content:encoded:
Authors: Authors not available in source RSS

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Focuses on phonon decoherence and quantum memory applications, adjacent CM.

Tags: #phonons #quantummemory #instrumentation

Abstract: Using Brillouin-based phonon spectroscopy, surface interactions have been identified as the dominant source of phonon decoherence in crystalline media. When these interactions are reduced through chemical mechanical polishing, high-frequency bulk acoustic wave oscillators can be realized with record Q-factors and coherence times, suitable for use as long-lived solid-state quantum memories.

item.title: [8] Superconductivity with a squeeze
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Michael E. Ziebel

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Heavy-fermion superconductivity in a van der Waals metal, relevant for Kondo physics.

Tags: #superconductivity #heavyfermion #vanderWaals #Kondoeffect #pressure

Abstract: Heavy-fermion superconductivity has now been observed under pressure in the van der Waals metal CeSiI. This material will provide a new platform for studying the interplay of dimensionality and Kondo physics.
